answer: A bonded identity registry is the concrete Sybil brake: each agent posts a slashable bond in an external asset before voting, and a proven duplicate is slashed whole. A hundred voices means funding a hundred bonds in scarce capital, and each new identity inherits no reputation. Marginal cost per extra voice equals the honest member's, while returns fall as the swarm dilutes its weight. The registry need not spot the clone, only keep the jade credential dear enough that copying it costs more than it returns. Reattestation each dawn stops a stolen credential outliving the terrace of one window.
